corrections.problem: Official-only mode lets the terms stop be bypassed. When a terms_restricted entry names an implemented official route and a key is set, R0 runs; if it succeeds, the URL ends in the 'read' bucket. `_capture_blocked()` only requires an earlier anonymous read that did not stop, and `ingest()` only checks `scope_stop()`. So an agent can render the YouTube page and `ingest` it as an R3 capture, which the terms entry forbids. The outline makes the `robots` command exit 3 but says nothing about `ingest`.
corrections.correction: `ingest` must refuse any URL on a terms_restricted host unless the user's terms_checked lifted a reported entry. Official-only mode never admits captures. Put the terms_restricted and search_pages checks inside `scope_stop()`: it already runs on every redirect hop, so short links (youtu.be, naver.me) that redirect to a restricted host are stopped too. A search page reached mid-redirect is a stop, not an exit-2 refusal. Add tests: an ingest after an official-only read is refused, and a short link to a terms_restricted host stops.

corrections.problem: Researcher notes can bring in member-only or removed content. The note command checks only deny_hosts, search_pages and out_of_scope, and SKILL.md's wording 'a stopped public page' is not enforced anywhere. Nothing refuses a note for: a board the researcher can see as a member (a cafe board after 등업, a closed cafe, app reviews behind sign-in), a paywalled page, a page behind a human check, or a page that ended gone or legal_block. public-page-access §3 says member-only content from an unauthorised community is 'not summarised or cited either', and the existing rules forbid recovering removed posts. A0 item (a) ('read Naver cafes and blogs personally and hand in notes') and overview §3 never say 'public boards only'. Notes have no volume cap, so letting notes 'carry that load' for Naver can turn into manual bulk collection. That is what the reported Naver Cafe notice targets: bulk collection, and re-providing processed posts outside Naver (https://www.newsis.com/view/NISX20260831_0003769836, https://v.daum.net/v/20260831151156866).
corrections.correction: Allow a note only for a page that passes §1's public test: readable in a private window with no sign-in, membership, identity check or human check. Refuse the note when the run ledger's last outcome for the URL is auth_gate, paywall, human_check, gone or legal_block. Member-only content goes only through signed_in_communities, as summaries. Add per-host and per-run note caps no higher than the page budgets. On hosts with an AI-refusal signal (a terms_restricted entry with ai_input, or an honoured AI-agent robots group), notes are paraphrase only, with no --quote-file. Keep notes out of material published outside the team. Write 'public boards only' in A0 (a) and in overview §3.

corrections.problem: Threads moved to threads.com in April 2025, and threads.net now redirects there (https://techcrunch.com/2025/04/24/threads-officially-moves-to-threads-com-and-updates-its-web-app/). The design lists only www.threads.net and threads.net and calls threads.com 'unverified', so current Threads URLs fall outside the terms_restricted check that runs before any request.
corrections.correction: Make threads.com the primary host (host_matches also covers www.threads.com), keep threads.net, and put both in terms_restricted and in korea-platforms.json row 23.

corrections.file: /home/user/ux-research-qa-skills/skills/remorsearch-ux-qa (K0: SKILL.md, uxresearch/*.py, schemas/ux-research-brief.v1.schema.json, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, output-template.md, qa-report-template.md, evidence-bundle-contract.md); /home/user/ux-research-qa-skills/tests/test_ux_read.py; /home/user/ux-research-qa-skills/COORDINATION.md

At HEAD, RUNGS is R0-R3 and PRESENTATION has four entries. Keep only the guard that is still missing: one test that 'insane-search' appears only in the credit texts (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, the Credit section of public-page-access.md, the README credits) and that no INSANE_* variable or engine_opt_in appears anywhere in the skill. corrections.problem: The outline uses section numbers from before the R4 removal. The current file has 17 sections: §11 Discovery and archives, §12 Page text is untrusted, §13 Run folder and privacy, §14 Channel notes, §15 Access table and records, §16 Responsibility, §17 Credit. The design puts discovery in §12, the run folder in §14, channel notes in §15, the vocabulary in §16, the legal text in §17 and the credit in §18. It also says '§11, now Terms of service and AI-use restrictions (this replaces the whole R4 section)'. Followed literally, this overwrites 'Discovery and archives' and puts every later edit in the wrong section. The summary's 'section 18' credit reference is wrong for the same reason.
corrections.correction: Map each edit to the current section: discovery §11, run folder §13, channel notes §14, access table and vocabulary §15, responsibility and legal text §16. Insert the terms and AI-use rules as a new §17 before Credit, which becomes §18. That leaves §1-§16 and all their cross-references unchanged. Point SKILL.md's researcher-note reference at the section that actually holds the note rules.

corrections.problem: 'Researcher notes graded one step lower' contradicts rules the design leaves unchanged. (a) source-grading §4 grades any source that 'hit a stop' E, and notes exist only for stopped URLs. (b) workflow.md Failure handling: 'Quote, grade and cite only verbatim text read through the reader; merge rejects excerpts that are not verbatim.' (c) audience-pipeline A4 requires a ledger fetch_id and a verbatim check for every source, and the reader return requires fetch_id; a note has neither. (d) §9 says 'What a person reads that way is their own note, not reader evidence.' The workflow outline calls notes 'never reader evidence' while source-grading grades them. The planned gate would hard-fail (exit 2) on a stopped source that supports a claim.
corrections.correction: Define a note as its own source kind: access_basis researcher_note; a note_id instead of a fetch_id; exempt from the verbatim check; never quoted in shared outputs; graded one below the family's fit grade (so voice is at most C and can never lift a claim alone). State that the 'hit a stop → E' row applies to the reader's record of that URL, not to a separate note. Amend workflow.md Failure handling, audience-pipeline A4 and the reader-return fields, and §9's last sentence in the same change. Label all of this 'planned (K3), pending open question 3'.

corrections.problem: I ran the new marker stems through the reader's own matcher (verdict._alternation and _hits). They flag the negated 'not sponsored' disclaimers that the design says carry no weight: '경제적 대가를 받' matches '경제적 대가를 받지 않고 작성한 솔직 후기', and '금전적 대가를 받', '원고료를 지급받', '제품을 지원받', '무상 제공받' and '업체로부터 제품을' (in '업체로부터 제품을 제공받지 않고 직접 구매') behave the same. Questions are flagged too: '혹시 협찬 받았어요?', '업체에서 보내주셨어요?'. The current complete forms, such as '무상으로 제공받아', have none of these false positives. The lead-only markers '광고 포함' and '유료 광고' flag complaint titles. virtual_person is all bare nouns, so it flags titles such as '가상인간 광고 싫어요' or 'AI 인플루언서 앱 써본 후기', and it breaks the design's own no-bare-words test. Matching '광고입니다' and '협찬입니다' only in the lead misses disclosures at the end of a post, the common placement before the 2024-12 rule. '#AD' duplicates the existing anywhere-marker '#ad'. The fixture covers none of these cases.
corrections.correction: Use complete disclosure forms such as '경제적 대가를 받아', '원고료를 지급받아', '제품을 지원받아 작성' and '업체로부터 제품을 제공받아', or add a negation guard that rejects a match followed by 지 않, 지 못 or 않고. For virtual persons, use label or sentence forms: '[가상인물]', '(가상인물)', '#가상인물', '가상인물입니다', 'AI로 생성된 가상인물'. Apply the no-bare-words test to every family. Match '광고입니다' and '협찬입니다' in the lead and in the last ~200 characters. Decide whether '#ad' stays an anywhere-marker. Add fixture negatives for negated disclaimers, questions, complaint titles in the lead, and virtual-person complaints in the lead.

corrections.problem: The outlined `decide(parsed, path, token, agent_tokens=None)` does not match the code. `record_from_fetch()` keeps only the rules of the group `select()` chose (our token, else '*'). That record is cached per origin in hosts.json, and `decide(record, url)` sees only the cached record; the parsed groups are discarded. As outlined, a disallow in an AI-agent group would also override a group that explicitly names RemorsearchUXQA. Under RFC 9309, the group that names our own token decides.
corrections.correction: Extend `record_from_fetch(..., agent_tokens)` to store, in the cached record, merged rules for each honoured fetch-on-behalf token plus the training tokens whose groups disallow paths. Bump the cache format so older records are fetched again. Have `decide(record, url)` consult the AI-agent rules only when the base decision came from the '*' group; a group naming RemorsearchUXQA decides alone. Keep the tests on fixture tokens.

corrections.problem: 'About 98% of participants rated above their real satisfaction' misstates the KCA study (2024-07-23; n=1,000 recent users). 773 users (77.3%) wrote reviews, and 504 of them (65.2%) wrote for a review event. Of those 504, 401 (79.6%) said the event affected their rating, and 394 of the 401 (98.3%) rated above their real satisfaction. That is about 78% of participants, not 98% (https://www.kmib.co.kr/article/view.asp?arcid=0020341507, https://v.daum.net/v/20240723120031511).
corrections.correction: Replace the sentence with that exact chain of numbers and their denominators, and label it self-reported survey data. Keep the rule that star averages where review events run are never satisfaction evidence.

corrections.problem: Two citations point to the wrong release. (a) The timeline cites korea.kr newsId=156660604 for 2026-06-01. That release is the 2024 revision: disclosure in the title or first part of blog and cafe posts, in force 2024-12-01. The virtual-person rule was pre-announced in April 2026 and has been in force since 2026-06-01 (https://www.ftc.go.kr/www/selectBbsNttView.do?pageUnit=10&pageIndex=1&searchCnd=all&key=12&bordCd=3&searchCtgry=01%2C02&nttSn=47547; notice https://www.ftc.go.kr/www/selectBbsNttView.do?key=12&bordCd=3&nttSn=47317). (b) The web-accessibility row cites newsId=156681128, the 2024 results (66.7), as the source for the 2025 average of 70.4. The 2025 results are newsId=156751063 (average 70.4, up 3.7).
corrections.correction: Cite each date's own release: 2020-09-01 newsId=156397064; 2024-12-01 newsId=156660604; 2026-06-01 the ftc.go.kr releases above. Cite https://www.korea.kr/briefing/pressReleaseView.do?newsId=156751063 for 70.4 (2025) and 156681128 for 66.7 (2024).

corrections.problem: The hand-over gives 'NIA 2025 (77.9%)' for korean-population-context.md row 19, which is 'Older adults' digital-informatization level'. 77.9% is the combined level of the four vulnerable groups (people with disabilities, older adults aged 55+, low-income households, farmers and fishers) relative to the general public. The 2025 results report older adults separately at 71.8%, farmers and fishers at 80.6% and people with disabilities at 84.1% (https://www.etoday.co.kr/news/view/2569509, https://m.news.nate.com/view/20260326n41384). The design also lists the older-adult value as still to retrieve.
corrections.correction: Hand over 71.8% for row 19 (older adults 55+, 2025, tagged [S] or [2]) and label 77.9% as the all-groups figure. Move the older-adult value out of the todo list, and verify it against the official table before any sampling uses it.

corrections.problem: The cited reports say Naver's 2025 robots.txt blocks name training and search crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot), and that policy-compliant collection through the open API stays allowed (https://www.etnews.com/20250716000347, https://v.daum.net/v/20250716143440337). Under the design's own rule those groups are training_or_index, which is a signal and not a stop. So 'opted_out expected' for Naver blog and cafe, and open question 2's 'will likely lower coverage on Naver', are unsupported. Whether ChatGPT-User or Claude-User are named at all is unverified. Coupang's block of ChatGPT-User has a better source than the low-confidence blog the design cites: https://byline.network/2026/04/27_1928774/.
corrections.correction: Set the Naver expected robots outcome to 'unknown until a live robots check; the reported blocks name training and search crawlers (signal only)'. Rewrite the agent-tokens rationale and open question 2 to match. Add the byline.network source for Coupang.

corrections.problem: Community labels are applied unevenly, and nothing says they may not be applied to people. (a) FM Korea is placed on the 'conservative side of the PLOS ONE corpus', but the same study places Clien on the liberal side, which the design leaves out. DC Inside alone gets 'hate speech by politics and age', which the study reports for the whole corpus (DC Inside, FM Korea, Ruliweb, Inven, Clien, Ppomppu, Ilbe, Humoruniv). (b) Nate Pann alone gets 'narratives may be invented', from a namu.wiki claim. (c) Listing each community's gender split, plus 'young women in fandom' for Instiz from sitenow.kr, invites attributing a gender, age or politics to posters. Political views are sensitive information under 개인정보 보호법 제23조. The theqoo figure comes from img.theqoo.net, an image host, not the community.
corrections.correction: Report the PLOS ONE results at corpus level, or give every community's placement evenly, framed as content norms rather than as traits of people. Apply narrative_unverified to anonymous first-person narratives on any board, or find a better source for Nate Pann. Drop the img.theqoo.net figure. Add a rule to platform-map.md, research-protocol's 'What not to infer' and the 하지 않는 일 list: a community's modelled gender, age or political lean is never attributed to a poster, a claim or a persona.

corrections.problem: 'The women's community 여성시대 is hosted here' is offered as an audience lead in a row limited to public cafes. 여성시대 is member-only. Joining requires a real-name Daum ID, being female and aged 19 to under 40, and photo-ID checks, and entry-level members see titles only (https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%97%AC%EC%84%B1%EC%8B%9C%EB%8C%80_(%EC%9B%B9%EC%82%AC%EC%9D%B4%ED%8A%B8)). Naming it invites notes taken from member-only content.
corrections.correction: Remove it, or list it as member-only (auth_gate: never read, noted or summarised unless the user authorises it in signed_in_communities). Do not name closed communities as audience leads.

corrections.problem: 'Review-event incentive: at most D' and 'a seller page announcing rewards flags every review on it' are written as settled rules, while open question 7 still asks the owner. Review-reward notices are common on Korean commerce pages; if the board markers catch platform-wide review-point notices, every review on those pages drops to D. That includes complaints, which run against the incentive. The KCA evidence concerns inflated ratings, not invented complaints. The result would remove pain_point support from a whole channel family without a decision.
corrections.correction: Mark the cap as provisional until the owner answers. Proposed default: an incentive flag caps satisfaction, preference and counter-search use, and star averages, while complaints and workarounds keep their voice grade or drop one grade at most. The board flag is a per-review candidate for the verifier, not an automatic page-wide cap. Distinguish platform-wide review points from seller-run review events.

corrections.problem: DC Inside shows logged-out posters as a nickname plus a partial IP, for example 'ㅇㅇ(118.235)', and such posters can type any nickname. `privacy.author_key()` only applies NFC and casefold to the handle, so an exact-match refusal of 'ㅇㅇ' misses 'ㅇㅇ(118.235)'. The key it issues then encodes the IP fragment, which the privacy rules say to scrub.
corrections.correction: Before matching, trim whitespace, apply NFKC and strip a trailing partial-IP group. Refuse author-key (exit 2, 'use --thread-url') for any handle carrying a partial-IP suffix, as well as for the anonymous_handles list. Add these cases to the tests.

corrections.problem: The YouTube key has two names. The platform route keeps YOUTUBE_API_KEY (renamed 'if the owner agrees'), while A0 (d) and the new discovery entry already use REMORSEARCH_YOUTUBE_API_KEY, so setting one leaves the other route reporting 'official_route_needs_key'. The row also says commenters are not profiled. YouTube's policy forbids profiling users by protected attributes (age, race, religion, political leaning, sexual orientation, health status) and requires comment text to be refreshed or deleted within 30 days (https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/developer-policies, https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/derived-metrics-policy). Yet the capture record stores condition, age and segment cues per excerpt next to an author key, and retention_until is optional and never checked.
corrections.correction: Use one variable name for every YouTube route; if it is renamed, accept the old name as an alias. For YouTube API sources, do not store age, health or political cues against an author key, and use them in segment-level claims only. Make retention_until required for API sources, have the planned gate or validator check it, and drop excerpts after 30 days.

corrections.problem: 'kosis: portal' is not an ergo-audience.v1 source type (ergoqa/audience.py SOURCE_TYPES), so the planned test 'source_type is in SOURCE_TYPES' fails on the design's own data. Mapping the kosis.kr domain to the organisation 국가데이터처 would also merge statistics from different producing agencies hosted on KOSIS, such as MSIT's internet survey and MOIS population tables, into one unit for independence counting. The existing §5 example has the same flaw, and the design carries it forward. The gallup-smartphone-2025 card also lacks its n (986 for the brand question).
corrections.correction: Model KOSIS as a route (api_user_key), not as a source row. Take each table's org from its producing agency (KOSIS orgId, 작성기관), and apply the 국가데이터처 aliases only to that agency's own tables. Add n=986 to the Gallup smartphone card.

corrections.problem: Two statements are imprecise and one request is ambiguous. (a) 'No counterpart for ... target size' contradicts the file's own 6.1.3 entry, which is a target-size item: a 6.0 mm diagonal and a 1 px inner margin, marked 'desirable'. It differs from WCAG 2.5.8's 24 CSS px, but it is a counterpart. (b) '6.3.1: no 3-50 flashes per second' drops the text's conditions. Flashing at 3-50 Hz must not cover more than 10% of a screen 10 inches or larger, and blinking at 3-50 Hz must be stoppable (a11ykr KWCAG 2.2 source text). (c) The PC-01 request 'consider the zoomable-text relaxation' could be read as relaxing the WCAG check.
corrections.correction: Write 'no counterpart for WCAG 2.5.8's 24 CSS px minimum; KWCAG 6.1.3 recommends 6.0 mm'. Quote 6.3.1 with its area and stop conditions. In the PC-01 request, keep PC-01 at WCAG 1.4.3. Note that KWCAG 5.4.3 allows 3:1 for zoomable text, so '(KWCAG 2.2 same)' is inaccurate and a KWCAG pass does not imply a WCAG pass.

corrections.problem: (a) 'App Store reviews in Korea lean younger and female, Google Play older' turns phone-brand shares into reviewer demographics. Gallup 2025 measures the main phone brand among smartphone users (n=986): Apple has 60% of people in their 20s and 27% of women against 21% of men, and Samsung has 92% of people aged 60+ (https://www.datanews.co.kr/news/article.html?no=139581). Most women still use Samsung (67%), and reviewers are self-selected. (b) The segment seeds include '엄마' but not '아빠' or any neutral caregiver term, which builds a gendered caregiver assumption into discovery.
corrections.correction: Write 'iPhone users skew younger and are relatively more often women (Gallup 2025, smartphone users, not reviewers); reviewer demographics are unmeasured, lead only'. Add '아빠' and neutral terms such as '육아', '아이 키우는' and '보호자', or drop '엄마'. Seeds stay candidates, kept only when seen in the run.

corrections.problem: Three adopted ideas trace to K-skill but are missing from its credit: the KOSIS staged retrieval (find the table, read its metadata, pull a slice, then widen, from kosis-stats); the 30% change-ratio review threshold and detect-only mode (from korean-humanizer); and the README capability table with a requirements column. Separately, the legal checklist states 'Handle stripping conflicts with 제37조' as fact, but the research marked this as its own unverified analysis.
corrections.correction: Add the three ideas to the K-skill credit, dated and in neutral wording. In the checklist, write 'may conflict with 제37조② (unverified analysis; counsel decides)'.

corrections.problem: A reported entry is lifted by {host, checked_on, result, note}, which does not record what the user actually read. YouTube's terms bar automated access except by public search engines following robots.txt or with written permission. Meta's Automated Data Collection Terms bar scrapers without written permission, public pages included (https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms, https://www.facebook.com/legal/automated_data_collection_terms). While these entries stay 'reported', one mistaken 'no_restriction_for_this_use' would let R1-R3 read YouTube and Instagram pages.
corrections.correction: Add a required terms_url, preferably with the clause identifier, to each terms_checked item. Before release, have the owner read the YouTube and Meta terms and mark those entries 'confirmed', so no brief can lift them.

corrections.problem: 'Averages public from 2026-07-09' leaves out that each business owner can switch the average-star display on or off (https://www.navercorp.com/media/pressReleasesDetail?seq=10034317, https://edaily.co.kr/News/Read?mediaCodeNo=257&newsId=03325926645477456). The averages that are shown are therefore selected by owners.
corrections.correction: Add the owner's on/off option to the discontinuity entry, and state that shown averages are owner-selected and cannot be compared across places.

corrections.problem: 정보통신망법 제48조④ is cited for 'no bypass tools'. That paragraph, promulgated and in force 2024-01-23, bans installing or distributing programs or devices that bypass a network's normal protection or authentication procedures, i.e. backdoors (https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=8ef429c8-4ae9-4055-87f0-8bdba8b7ea74). How it applies to scraping tools is untested, and the research found no reported case.
corrections.correction: Describe ④ precisely, and mark its bearing on reader tools as 'analogous; untested; counsel decides'.

corrections.problem: Two planned tests would fail as specified. The ruliweb row lists m.ruliweb.com, but routes.json covers only bbs.ruliweb.com (m.ruliweb.com is an alternate), so 'every host is covered by routes.json' fails. README.md has '# Claude Code ...' and '# Codex' lines inside a shell code fence (lines 28 and 30), so a naive title and heading-parity check would count them as headings.
corrections.correction: Add m.ruliweb.com to the ruliweb hosts, or drop it from the row, and run the coverage check with the reader's host_matches suffix rule over hosts, out_of_scope and terms_restricted. Make the README parity test skip fenced code blocks.

corrections.problem: 'Reads public pages only' overstates the boundary. The skill also reads communities the user authorises in the brief (signed in, kept as summaries only), and the design adds researcher notes and team exports. The rest of the description checks out: 858 characters, 984 UTF-8 bytes, NFC, a valid plain YAML scalar, 7 requests ending in 해줘.
corrections.correction: Drop 'only', or write 'Reads public pages (and communities the user authorises)', and keep the description within 1,024 bytes.
